text:
ryan: Heads up — during the keystore rotation window in us-west1 a subset of BMCs failed to persist NVRAM writes. About 18 nodes left the canary pool and some machines toggled UEFI lockdown, so provisioning is backing up. Anyone on watch?

sophia: saw the same. provisioning queue spiked ~09:12 UTC and allocate-agent retried. GPUs in the affected racks are stuck in 'awaiting-boot' state.

infra-bot: ALERT: 18 nodes (rack-usw1-*-02..-19) removed from canary pool. Reason: BMC NVRAM write error (ERR_NVRAM_STORE).

amy: @ryan @sophia can you paste the ipmi logs? curious if this is the keystore signing failing or an unrelated flash glitch. :eyes:

ryan: here's a trimmed ipmi dump and journal snippet from one affected node:```
IPMI: fwstore: write failed: -5
kernel: efivars: write to variable failed (Permission denied)
systemd: cloud-init started provisioning but returned non-zero
```

dennis: this smells like the new key material didn't land in the BMC's keystore and the firmware rejected the variable write (UEFI lockdown fallback). Took a look at the rotation job — it pushed keys to vault then called the batch agent. Some hosts timed out during the HSM unwrap.

amy: if HSM unwrap is the culprit we might have partial rotations where BMCs have new pubkey fingerprint but no matching private material accessible, so they reject NV writes.

ryan: current impact: 18 nodes (~72 A100 GPUs) offline for provisioning, 12 nodes in eu-west1 on canary unaffected. Allocation backlog causing autoscaler to spin up extra spot capacity as fallback — rough estimate +$9/hr so far.

sophia: quick mitigation: can we flip the rollout to "allow-shim" (install signed shim/grub to bypass lockdown) for canary only, so provisioning can finish while we rollback keystore changes? Risk: temporary reduced attestation guarantees.

dennis: agreed option A: enable shim for canary and pause keystore rotation. Option B: revert rotation and push previous keystore version. Option C: manual per-rack HSM rewrap (slow). I'm leaning revert first if we can do it quickly.

amy: revert path validated for account with steps: 1) stop rotation job 2) re-publish previous keystore to BMCs via oob-agent 3) kick canary reprovision. We have a runbook but it requires jumphost access.

ryan: I can jump in the jumphost. Scheduling rollback now, ETA ~20m for first rack. I'll disable canary assignments for the affected slot to avoid churn.

infra-bot: ACTION CREATED: #ticket-1187 keystore-rotation-rollback (assignee: dennis).

dennis: starting rollback for rack-usw1-02..-07 now. Will stream logs to the runbook channel.

amy: if rollback stalls, fallback is to enable shim for provisioning only: feature-flag redwood.oob.allow-shim=true on canary route. We should get exec approval for prod change though.

ryan: got partial success — first 6 nodes reprovisioning. Provision queue dropped by ~30%. Keeping rollback until all 18 are green, then we'll re-run rotation with longer HSM timeout and per-rack pacing.

dennis: note for postmortem: add a canary step that verifies efivars writes after keystore install and before promoting to wider fleet. Also instrument BMC keystore apply latency metric.

ryan: +1. Also let's add cost guardrails to avoid autoscaler spinning extra spot GPUs for >15m for these types of failures.

amy: filing a small follow-up: runbook update + telemetry dashboard card for keystore_apply_latency. Will assign to infra-instrumentation.

dennis: rollback finished for all racks, all 18 nodes back in canary. provisioning backlog cleared. Re-running rotation with 60s per-host unwrap timeout and sequential per-rack logic.

ryan: great work everyone. Leave the ticket open for the follow-ups. :thumbsup:
